input.quote: 9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.
input.rationale: There is no indemnification section anywhere in the Agreement: the outline runs from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), and no clause imposes any defence, indemnity or hold-harmless duty on Vendor (or on Customer). Several provisions nonetheless assume indemnities exist - Section 9.3 cross-refers to "the remedies required by Section 20.5", Section 19.4 preserves remedies for "indemnified claims", Section 21.3 treats "its indemnification obligations" as Excluded Claims, and Section 30.5 preserves "vested indemnity rights" - so the dangling cross-reference confirms the section is simply absent. That is walk-away territory (no Vendor IP indemnity at all). We insert a new Section 20.1 at the preferred level after Section 19.5: Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates against third-party claims for IP infringement by the Services or Deliverables, Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorised access to Customer Data, and Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with notice, defence-control and cooperation mechanics, and any Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law. We deliberately did not take the fallback, because its 3x-annual-fees super-cap would cut across Section 21.3, which currently leaves indemnification obligations uncapped in our favour. Note for the negotiation: Section 9.3's reference to Section 20.5 remedies (procure, modify, replace) remains unsupported; we can add those IP remedies if Vendor prefers to renumber rather than conform Section 9.3.

proposal.summary: Insert missing Vendor indemnity (Section 20) covering IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach and wilful misconduct, with standard procedure and a narrow Customer indemnity limit.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no indemnity section even though Sections 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 assume one (9.3 cross-refers to a non-existent Section 20.5), so we add the Vendor defence and indemnity our playbook requires, with notice, defence-control and cooperation mechanics and a limit on any Customer indemnity.

ops.text: Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Customer shall give Vendor prompt written notice of the claim, Vendor shall control its defence and settlement, and Customer shall provide reasonable cooperation. Customer's indemnification obligations, if any, are limited to third-party claims arising out of Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law.
